newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo to face slow return to world capital markets.
newsitem.headline: Yugo to face slow return to world capital markets.

text.p: Yugoslav central bank Vice-Governor Zarko Trbojevic has cautioned that a return to world capital markets would be a slow and difficult process, the Belgrade daily Politika Ekspres said on Friday.

"A huge and difficult task is ahead of us before we return to the UN and then to the IMF, World Bank, WTO in order to conclude convenient agreements with the Paris club and the so-called London Club of creditors," Politika Ekspres quoted Trbojevic as saying.
Trbojevic said it will take some time before Yugoslavia regains hold of its hard currency and gold reserves as well as securities deposited with banks in over 40 countries around the world.

"We will have to wait for those first hot German marks, dollars, guilders, swiss francs and the rest of capital needed to stimulate production and exports and clear the first tranche of overdue payments" he told Politika Ekspres in an interview.
Trbojevic said "First of all we must conclude succession and divide assets with former Yugoslavia's republics. That will be a slow and difficult process."

According to Trbojevic, difficulties were clearly signalled after the French authorities last week decided to freeze again NBY's hard currency and gold reserves until a final decision on division of that capital is reached."
According to some estimates, almost $650 million is in dispute.
It is still unclear whether other countries and their central and commercial banks would follow suit.
"The most important thing is that we calmly and without unrealistic optimism turn to restoring ties with foreign banks, first of all with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS)," he said.
BIS support is the key, because relations with any country, its central bank and commercial banks depend on it, he added.
